old_caption: The video captures a static scene featuring a large cylindrical object, possibly a concrete block or a similar heavy structure, resting on a bed of loose dirt and debris. A hammer with a yellow handle and black head is positioned at the base of the cylinder, beneath it. In the top left corner of the frame, three individuals are visible, observing the scene. They appear engaged. The background is blurred, suggesting a focus on the objects in the foreground. The overall atmosphere suggests an outdoor setting.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene where a large cylindrical object, possibly a concrete block or a similar heavy structure, is being struck by a hammer. The hammer, with its yellow handle and black head, is positioned at the base of the cylinder, which is resting on a bed of loose dirt and debris. As the hammer strikes, it causes the cylinder to tilt slightly, sending up a cloud of dust and debris into the air. The background is blurred, suggesting a focus on the action in the foreground. In the top left corner of the frame, three individuals are visible, observing the event. They appear engaged and possibly amused by the spectacle. The overall atmosphere suggests an outdoor setting, likely a construction site or a similar environment. The video emphasizes the force of the impact and the resulting dust cloud, highlighting the power of the hammer against the heavy object.
caption: The video captures a slow crushing sequence in a static close-up. A large silver-grey metal cylinder, marked by a horizontal weld seam and a raised bottom rim, occupies the center of the frame. It hovers just above a claw hammer lying on a surface strewn with reddish-brown rubble and white fragments in front of a yellow-and-black hazard-striped platform edge. Throughout the excerpt the cylinder translates steadily downward, its rim closing the gap above the hammer. The black head and claw, clearly visible early on, become progressively hidden until only a thin sliver remains. A small plume of dust at the right base of the cylinder persists and thickens slightly as the descent continues. In a top-left picture-in-picture inset, three men in caps watch from outdoors under a blue sky, their broad smiles giving way to more focused, squinting expressions while the left man leans downward. The rubble and hazard stripe stay fixed, confirming the cylinder's motion rather than any camera movement.

without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
